claims.statement: drizzle.config.ts at the repository root pins the Drizzle schema source to ./lib/db/schema.ts, the migration output directory to ./lib/db/migrations, the SQL dialect to 'postgresql', and the database URL to process.env.POSTGRES_URL, making lib/db/schema.ts the single source of truth for both runtime queries and migration generation.

lib/db/client.ts exports the database client as a lazy JavaScript Proxy that defers opening the postgres connection until the first property access, and throws 'POSTGRES_URL environment variable is required' when that environment variable is unset, so importing the module never throws and only the first query surfaces a missing URL.

Every per-user child table (accounts, keys, connectors, tasks, settings) declares a foreign key from its user_id column to users.id with onDelete: 'cascade', and task_messages.task_id declares a foreign key to tasks.id with onDelete: 'cascade', so deleting a users row removes every account, key, connector, task, and setting the user owns in a single statement and deleting a task removes its conversation transcript automatically.

The schema enforces four one-per-X uniqueness invariants with btree unique indexes: users_provider_external_id_idx on users(provider, externalId), accounts_user_id_provider_idx on accounts(userId, provider), keys_user_id_provider_idx on keys(userId, provider), and settings_user_id_key_idx on settings(userId, key); tasks and task_messages carry no unique indexes beyond their primary keys.

tasks.logs is declared as a JSONB column typed as LogEntry[] (with type restricted to 'info' | 'command' | 'error' | 'success'), and tasks.mcpServerIds is declared as a JSONB column typed as string[]; the connector IDs in mcpServerIds are stored by value rather than via a foreign key so that deleting a connector does not cascade into tasks that referenced it.

The accounts.provider column is declared with the enum ['github'] and a default of 'github', meaning the accounts table is wired up only for linked GitHub identities today; the schema is structured so additional providers can be added later by extending the enum without further code changes beyond the Zod validators and the upsert paths.

lib/db/schema.ts re-exports the accounts table as userConnections and the Account / InsertAccount types as UserConnection / InsertUserConnection for backwards compatibility with code written before the table was renamed, so import { userConnections } and the UserConnection types resolve to the same Drizzle table instance and the same TypeScript types as their accounts counterparts.

upsertUser in lib/db/users.ts is the only writer to users and implements a three-tier identity merge: it first looks up users by (provider, externalId) and updates the existing row, then for GitHub sign-ins falls back to looking up accounts by (provider='github', externalUserId) so a user who originally signed in with Vercel and later signs in directly with GitHub converges on the same users row, and otherwise inserts a fresh nanoid()-keyed row with timestamps set to now.

lib/db/settings.ts exposes four helpers that read the settings table with a constant fallback: getSetting returns the raw string value or the supplied default, getNumericSetting parses it with parseInt(value, 10), and the two domain-specific wrappers getMaxMessagesPerDay and getMaxSandboxDuration wrap getNumericSetting around the MAX_MESSAGES_PER_DAY and MAX_SANDBOX_DURATION module constants from lib/constants.ts, with all four short-circuiting to the default when the userId argument is undefined.

Five sets of text columns hold secrets that are always encrypted with the AES-256-CBC primitive from lib/crypto.ts before write and decrypted on read: users.accessToken and users.refreshToken, accounts.accessToken and accounts.refreshToken, keys.value, and connectors.oauthClientSecret and connectors.env (the env column is a JSON object encrypted as a single string); the schema does not flag these columns as encrypted — the convention is enforced by every write call site.

Every table in lib/db/schema.ts is paired with two Zod schemas — an insertXxxSchema that validates payloads going into the database with defaults mirroring the Drizzle column defaults (selectedAgent defaults to 'claude', maxDuration defaults to parseInt(process.env.MAX_SANDBOX_DURATION || '300', 10), tasks.status defaults to 'pending', progress to 0, connector.type to 'remote', connector.status to 'disconnected') and a selectXxxSchema that mirrors the column nullability so nullable text columns come back as string | null, nullable integers as number | null, and nullable JSONB columns as T | null.

The connectors.env column undergoes a type change on the insert/select boundary: the insertConnectorSchema accepts a Record<string, string> (the unencrypted JSON object from the connector dialog), the column stores the AES-256-CBC-encrypted <iv_hex>:<ciphertext_hex> string, and selectConnectorSchema returns string | null reflecting the encrypted wire format; the application layer decrypts and JSON.parses the value at task execution time.

tasks.deletedAt is the soft-delete tombstone that distinguishes a user-removed task from a task that was stopped while running; it is written only by DELETE /api/tasks/:taskId, every task-scoped read in the system filters isNull(tasks.deletedAt), while a stopped task (status='stopped') remains fully readable and can be rewound via POST /api/tasks/:taskId/continue.

The schema migration workflow edits lib/db/schema.ts, runs pnpm db:generate to produce a new numbered SQL file under lib/db/migrations, and applies the migration locally with pnpm db:migrate; in production scripts/migrate-production.ts runs the same drizzle-kit migrate but only when VERCEL_ENV === 'production', so schema changes ride along with production deploys but no-op on preview and local environments.
